items.block:
The term <term>Bhagavan</term> also refers to "possessing" <note>the Tibetan "ldan" in "bcom ldan 'das"</note> the six perfections:
Lordship, excellent form,
Glory, fame, wisdom,
And perfect diligence;
Possessing these six is called "Possessing."

items.before:
Lordship and good form,
Glory, fame, and primordial wisdom,
And the perfection of diligence;
These six are called "fortunes."
items.after:
Sovereignty and fine form,
Glory, fame, primordial wisdom,
And perfect diligence:
These six are what 'endowed' means."

items.block:
Furthermore, he is the Blessed One because he possesses <term>den</term> the six qualities such as sovereignty. Regarding that, it is said:
Sovereignty and beautiful form,
Splendor, fame, and wisdom,
And perfect diligence:
One who possesses these six is so named.

This is the empowerment for abandoning the mental afflictions.

items.block:
As for the effect that is born, is it something not empty or something empty that is produced? In that regard:
An effect that is not empty will not be born. 
That which is not empty will not cease. 
That which is not empty would be 
Both unceasing and unborn.

Is not logically a thing.

items.block:
Suppose you wish to avoid this fault and claim that the stepping possesses going, and that the going itself is the act of going. Even then:
If the stepping were to possess a going,
Two goings would logically follow:
The one by which the stepping is defined,
And the going that exists within it.
